target_customer: US-incorporated companies operated from abroad, especially Latin American startups
problem: Foreign-run companies struggle to get US dollar accounts, payments, cards and treasury. Blinka provides USD accounts, cross-border transfers, cards and yield on idle cash through partner banks.
business_model: Fintech banking platform (not a bank) earning on payments, cards and treasury products

founders.name: Juan Pablo Linares
previous_startups: Built and sold products with his brother for about four years (unnamed)
founders.background_notes: Colombian lawyer in M&A and litigation; D1 soccer player; angel investor in 15+ startups per YC page. College not stated.

founders.name: Sebastian Linares
founders.background_notes: Brother of the CEO per press; led credit risk modeling team at Virginia Tech per YC page.

competitors.name: Mercury
competitors.what: US startup banking, accessible to some non-resident founders
competitors.funding_then: reported conditional OCC charter approval April 2026 (wiki claim)

technical_complexity.rationale: Built on partner banks (Portage Bank, Third National, Atomic Invest) so the work is compliance, onboarding and product integration rather than core infrastructure.

defensibility.rationale: Bank accounts stick once opened, but BaaS partners make the stack replicable and larger neobanks can court the same customers.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent action specific to Blinka recorded.

market_need_then: Colombian press reports more than 150 businesses in accounts opened or applications and over US$10M processed in the first two months (outlet claims); foreign-owned LLCs are commonly rejected by US neobanks per comparison guides.

identity.logo: Separate light and dark mode logos
identity.visual_style: Clean minimal layout with clear disclosures
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and plain: Banking, without borders

branding.community_and_virality: Covered by several Colombian and LatAm outlets as a Colombian-founded YC company

brand_strength.rationale: Distinctive short name with LatAm press attention, but little brand-specific evidence and an unrelated Blinka dating brand trademark exists.

outcome_analysis: Blinka is a Fall 2026 company with early traction claims in Latin American press and no confirmed outside round. It is active and too new for an outcome. Its risks are dependence on partner banks and competition from neobanks that serve foreign founders.
notes: Preqin shows a USD 20,000 funding in April 2025, paywalled and unverified; not recorded. Traction figures are from Spanish-language press and not independently verified. Team size reported around seven by one outlet. Founding year not stated; one outlet places founding in New York. Competitor sources are 2026 guides, not founding-era launch coverage.
